title: The application of machine learning for identifying frailty in older patients during hospital admission.
summary: Among 3,367 older inpatients, 2,843 were labeled frail; SVM achieved internal test AUROC 0.811, accuracy 73.15%, precision 94.53% and F1 82.10%. Age and routine clinical features ranked among influential predictors. Randomly held-out test set from the same single hospital and six-month data window; no external/prospective validation. The high frailty prevalence and single-center retrospective sample limit transfer; model performance is not proof of improved patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Compared logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost and SVM on routine admission-period clinical data; SHAP/PDP interpreted frailty predictions.
organization: Center for Geriatrics & Gerontology, Taichung Veterans General Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan

source_review.scope: The BMC primary full text reports a machine-learning frailty screen trained on 3,367 hospitalized older adults (2,843 frail); the internal test set gave SVM AUROC 0.811, accuracy 73.15%, precision 94.53% and F1 82.10%, with age and routine clinical features important to predictions. This is a specific clinical screening result for acute-care inpatients. The first located result-bearing version is the publisher article dated 2024-09-27; exact-title/DOI searches found no earlier matching preprint, which does not establish global priority. Retrospective single-center design and internal testing limit generalization; no clinical utility or intervention benefit is claimed.
